data.narrative:
Halo is a Series B chip design company in the Semiconductors sector. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 5 private companies at the same or adjacent stage (SambaNova Systems, Rebellions, d-Matrix, Positron AI, and DEEPX) alongside 3 public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) for sector context.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-Progression applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to Halo's $122M total raised, implying $232M. Peer-Median derives valuation from the five comparable private companies, which show a median valuation of $2.0B and a range of $529M to $11.0B, yielding a $2.0B implied value. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied due to absence of revenue data, though the public semiconductor sector trades at a 20.5x price-to-sales median.

The two-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $197M to $2.3B, with a median of $1.1B. The wide spread reflects material heterogeneity in the peer set: SambaNova at $11.0B occupies a distinct upper tier, while stage advancement varies across comparables. Key uncertainties include the company's technical differentiation relative to $2B+ Series A peers, capital efficiency relative to total raised, and the sustainability of elevated semiconductor valuations. Revenue visibility would significantly narrow this range.
